cycleTypes.name: Eco / Light Wash (105°F–115°F / 40°C–46°C, No Heated Dry)
cycleTypes.description: Low thermal lethality; relies almost entirely on physical dilution and detergent surfactants. Ineffective against norovirus, hepatitis A, or heat-tolerant biofilms.

cycleTypes.name: Normal Residential Wash (120°F–130°F / 49°C–54°C, Air Dry)
cycleTypes.description: Standard residential baseline cycle. Achieves moderate reduction of light vegetative pathogens (2–3 logs) but fails against human norovirus or dried-on proteinaceous soil.

cycleTypes.name: Pots & Pans / Heavy Soil (140°F–145°F / 60°C–63°C, Heated Dry)
cycleTypes.description: Extended thermal exposure sufficient to eliminate Salmonella, E. coli, and Campylobacter, but marginal for non-enveloped viral capsids without high-alkaline oxygen bleach.

cycleTypes.name: NSF/ANSI 184 Certified Sanitize Cycle (155°F–160°F / 68°C–71°C Final Rinse)
cycleTypes.description: Official NSF/ANSI 184 residential sanitize cycle. Exceeds 150°F (65.6°C) minimum rinse with prolonged thermal dwell, guaranteeing ≥ 5-log (99.999%) reduction of vegetative pathogens and > 4-log norovirus inactivation.

cycleTypes.name: Commercial Warewasher High-Temp (NSF/ANSI 3: 160°F Wash, 180°F / 82°C Final Rinse)
cycleTypes.description: Commercial high-temperature restaurant warewasher. Achieves instantaneous thermal flash pasteurization across tableware within 60–90 seconds.

pathogens.name: Human Norovirus (GII.4) / Murine Norovirus (MNV-1)
pathogens.clinicalRisk: Acute viral gastroenteritis; extremely contagious, environmentally stable on dishware, resistant to mild surfactants and stomach acid.

pathogens.name: Salmonella enterica (Raw Poultry & Egg Pathogen)
pathogens.clinicalRisk: Salmonellosis, severe gastrointestinal infection, fever, systemic bacteremia in pediatric and geriatric individuals.

pathogens.name: Listeria monocytogenes (Deli Meat & Dairy Pathogen)
pathogens.clinicalRisk: Invasive listeriosis, meningitis, maternal-fetal sepsis, and spontaneous abortion with high mortality rate (20–30%).

pathogens.name: Escherichia coli (STEC O157:H7 - Ground Beef Pathogen)
pathogens.clinicalRisk: Hemorrhagic colitis, severe bloody diarrhea, and hemolytic uremic syndrome (HUS) leading to acute renal failure.

pathogens.name: Enterococcus faecium (NSF/ANSI 184 Regulatory Surrogate)
pathogens.clinicalRisk: Official NSF/ANSI 184 regulatory test organism used by laboratories to validate whether residential dishwashers qualify for the Sanitize label.

pathogens.name: Clostridium & Bacillus Endospores (Myth Debunker)
pathogens.clinicalRisk: Bacterial endospores survive boiling (100°C) and cannot be killed by ANY residential dishwasher cycle. Requires medical autoclave or pressure retort (121°C / 250°F).

detergentFormulations.name: High-Alkaline Powder / Pod with Sodium Percarbonate Bleach (pH 10.5–11.5)
detergentFormulations.description: Synergistic chemical disinfection. Sodium percarbonate dissolves into hydrogen peroxide and sodium carbonate at >50°C, oxidizing viral capsids and saponifying bacterial cell walls.

detergentFormulations.name: Standard Commercial Liquid / Gel Detergent (pH 8.0–9.0, Enzymes Only)
detergentFormulations.description: Contains proteases and amylases to break down starch and protein soil, but lacks oxidizing bleaches. Disinfection relies >90% on thermal water heat.

detergentFormulations.name: Eco / Plant-Based Neutral Liquid (pH 7.0–7.8, No Bleach)
detergentFormulations.description: Mild non-ionic plant surfactants without alkaline saponification or chemical oxidizers. Disinfection relies almost 98% on thermal pasteurization.

soilShieldingMatrices.name: Pre-Rinsed / Light Soil Film (Direct Water Contact)
soilShieldingMatrices.description: Thin aqueous biofilm; microorganisms are directly exposed to pressurized hot water jets and detergent chemistry.

soilShieldingMatrices.name: Greasy Lipid / Animal Tallow Layer (Hydrophobic Barrier)
soilShieldingMatrices.description: Hydrophobic fat film creates an insulating thermal and chemical barrier, retarding water penetration and increasing microbial survival time by 50%.

soilShieldingMatrices.name: Dried-On Egg / Cheese / Starch Matrix (Encapsulated)
soilShieldingMatrices.description: Dehydrated proteinaceous crust acts as a sacrificial shield, buffering pathogens from detergent alkalinity and requiring prolonged mechanical softening.

hydraulicLoadFactors.name: Properly Spaced & Unobstructed Spray Jets (100% Impingement)
hydraulicLoadFactors.description: Spray arms rotate freely and water jets reach all dishware surfaces with full rated pressure and thermal transfer.

hydraulicLoadFactors.name: Overcrowded / Nested Bowls (Shadowing Zone)
hydraulicLoadFactors.description: Bowls resting inside one another create hydrodynamic shadow zones where water cannot circulate, lowering local surface temperatures by 9°F (5°C).

hydraulicLoadFactors.name: Blocked Lower Spray Arm (Tall Item Occlusion)
hydraulicLoadFactors.description: A tall cookie sheet, spatula, or cutting board prevents the spray arm from spinning. 70% of the rack sits in a stagnant cold pool with near-zero disinfection.

presets.name: Household Norovirus Outbreak on NSF Sanitize Cycle
presets.description: Cleaning dishes used by a family member infected with active stomach flu (norovirus) using NSF/ANSI 184 Sanitize and oxygen bleach pod.

presets.name: Raw Chicken Cutting Board & Plate Washed on Eco Cycle
presets.description: High-risk Salmonella contamination washed with eco-friendly neutral detergent on low-temperature 42°C eco wash.

presets.name: Infant Baby Bottles & Teats on NSF Sanitize Cycle
presets.description: Sanitizing infant formula bottles and silicone nipples against Listeria and E. coli in residential dishwasher.

presets.name: Overcrowded Nested Bowls with Dried Cheese on Normal Wash
presets.description: Everyday normal wash with standard gel detergent and overcrowded bowls shielding Salmonella bacteria.

presets.name: Attempting to Sterilize C. Botulinum Spores in Dishwasher
presets.description: Home canning myth test: evaluating if running jars on Sanitize cycle kills Clostridium botulinum endospores.

sanitizationActionProtocols.title: Stomach Flu (Norovirus) Decontamination Protocol
sanitizationActionProtocols.action: Always select the certified 'Sanitize' cycle (or 'Hi-Temp Wash' + 'Heated Dry') and use a powder or multi-chamber pod containing sodium percarbonate (oxygen bleach). Avoid short eco-cycles or unheated dry modes.
sanitizationActionProtocols.rationale: Human norovirus is a resilient non-enveloped virus requiring at least 140°F–150°F (60°C–65.6°C) for several minutes. Standard 110°F–120°F cycles dilute the virus but leave viable particles on glass and cutlery surfaces that can cross-infect other family members.

sanitizationActionProtocols.title: The Stalled Spray Arm Check (Spin Before Starting)
sanitizationActionProtocols.action: Before closing the dishwasher door, give both the upper and lower spray arms a manual 360-degree spin with your hand to verify they rotate freely without striking tall cutting boards, baking sheets, or protruding ladle handles.
sanitizationActionProtocols.rationale: A physically blocked spray arm stops water distribution entirely. Dishes in the shadow zone receive no kinetic scouring and experience temperature drops of 20°F or more, resulting in near-total sanitation failure.

sanitizationActionProtocols.title: The Bacterial Endospore Limitation (Canning & Home Preservation)
sanitizationActionProtocols.action: NEVER rely on a dishwasher's 'Sanitize' cycle to sterilize canning jars for low-acid food preservation (beans, meats, soups, stocks). Always use an approved pressure canner at 240°F (115°C–121°C) under 10–15 PSI.
sanitizationActionProtocols.rationale: Dishwashers peak at ~160°F (71°C). Bacterial endospores from Clostridium botulinum survive boiling water (212°F / 100°C) for hours. A dishwasher sanitize cycle achieves ZERO log reduction of botulinum spores, leaving preserved food at risk of lethal toxin production.

sanitizationActionProtocols.title: Use Liquid Rinse Aid for Rapid Hydrophobic Water Shedding
sanitizationActionProtocols.action: Keep the dishwasher rinse aid dispenser full. Rinse aid lowers water surface tension, causing water to sheet off rapidly during final rinse rather than forming stagnant droplets.
sanitizationActionProtocols.rationale: Microorganisms require free moisture (a_w > 0.85) to survive and proliferate after a cycle finishes. Plates that dry completely within minutes deny residual bacteria the hydration needed to re-establish biofilms inside dark, humid dishwasher cabinets.
